title: Import blocks from a Cloud Asset Inventory export
scenario: Tessellate is bringing years of hand-built GCP resources under Terraform, project by project. Typing import blocks by hand is the toil: every resource type has its own import ID format, Google-managed service accounts and the default network must be left alone, and anything already in state must be skipped. You get a Cloud Asset Inventory export of tsl-riq-prod, the IDs Terraform already manages and a starter generator that handles networks and firewalls.
task: Map each supported asset type to its google provider resource and exact import ID (including project IAM members)
Skip the default network, Google-managed service accounts and service agent bindings; skip what state already has; report unsupported types
Group files by owner label (subnets inherit their network's owner) with valid, stable, collision-free identifiers
Output that parses as HCL and is byte-stable regardless of input order
acceptance: The export produces exactly the expected 13 import blocks in riq, mdm, riq-ml and platform files
The report lists skipped, unsupported and already-managed items
Same output for shuffled input; CLI writes the files
